requirement.rule: TTY detection must check the actual output stream being written to (stdout), not simply check for the presence of a `CI` or similar environment variable, since many legitimate interactive terminal sessions also happen to have CI-like env vars set (e.g. inside an interactive debugging session in a CI runner's shell), and the correct signal is genuinely about whether the terminal can render live-updating output.
requirement.scope: Detection mechanism for interactive vs non-interactive environments.

hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: A first draft checked for common CI environment variables (CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS, etc.) as a proxy for non-interactivity, which was reversed in favor of directly checking `sys.stdout.isatty()`, since the env-var heuristic produced both false positives and false negatives.

requirement.rule: The fallback plain-text progress logging must still respect `CURATOR_DISABLE_RICH_DISPLAY`'s existing tqdm-fallback behavior where applicable — this new non-TTY detection is an additional trigger for the same fallback path, not a third, separate progress-display mode to build and maintain.
requirement.scope: Code reuse: route through the existing tqdm fallback rather than building new plain-text logging.

tasks.title: Batch job cancellation on user interrupt
tasks.description: When a user presses Ctrl+C during a `batch=True` run while polling for job completion, offer to cancel the in-progress batch job on the provider's side rather than just exiting the local process and leaving the remote job running.

requirement.rule: On interrupt, the code must prompt the user interactively (yes/no) before cancelling the remote batch job, since the job may already be far along and the user might just want to detach and resume polling later rather than actually cancel and lose the (partially paid-for) in-progress work.
requirement.scope: Interrupt handling during the batch polling loop only.
requirement.exclusions_or_crossover: This confirmation prompt must be skipped (defaulting to 'do not cancel, just exit') when running in a non-interactive/non-TTY environment, since there's no one to answer the prompt and blocking forever on stdin would be worse than either choice.

hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: An early version cancelled the remote job automatically and immediately on any Ctrl+C with no prompt, which was reversed after a user lost hours of in-progress batch work from an accidental double Ctrl+C.

requirement.rule: If the user confirms cancellation, the persisted batch job ID (from the on-disk resume mechanism) must be cleared only after the provider confirms the cancellation succeeded, not immediately upon the user's 'yes' answer, so a failed cancellation attempt doesn't leave an orphaned job with no local record to resume polling it.
requirement.scope: Ordering between cancellation confirmation and local state cleanup.

tasks.title: Multimodal prompt token/cost estimation accuracy
tasks.description: Extend the pre-flight cost estimator to account for image tokens (not just text tokens) when a multimodal `response_format`/prompt is used, since images can dominate total token cost.

requirement.rule: Image token cost must be estimated using each provider's own documented image-tokenization formula (which vary — e.g. dimension-tile-based for some providers, flat-fee-per-image for others) rather than a single universal per-image flat estimate applied across all providers, since a universal flat estimate would be wildly inaccurate for providers that scale image cost with resolution.
requirement.scope: Image token estimation, per-provider.

hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: An early version used a single flat 'assume 1000 tokens per image' estimate across all providers for simplicity, which was reversed after it produced estimates off by an order of magnitude for high-resolution images on providers that tokenize by tile/resolution.

requirement.rule: For a provider whose exact image-tokenization formula isn't yet implemented in the estimator, the pre-flight estimate must clearly flag itself as a lower-bound/text-only estimate (via a printed caveat) rather than silently reporting a number that omits image costs entirely with no indication anything was left out.
requirement.scope: Fallback behavior for unimplemented provider formulas.
requirement.observability: Printed caveat must be visually distinct (e.g. a warning line) from the main estimate line.

tasks.title: Trainer config serialization for reproducibility logging
tasks.description: Log the full `TinkerTrainerConfig` / `FireworksTrainerConfig` used for a training run to a local file alongside the run's output, so users can later reproduce exactly what config produced a given fine-tuned model.

requirement.rule: The logged config must be the fully-resolved config (including any defaults that were auto-filled, like a default `learning_rate` Fireworks auto-selects) captured at the point training actually starts, not the config object as originally constructed by the user before any defaults were resolved — otherwise re-loading the logged config later wouldn't actually reproduce the same run if defaults changed between library versions.
requirement.scope: Timing and completeness of the logged config snapshot.

hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: An initial version logged the user's original config object immediately at TrainerConfig construction time, which was reversed once it was clear that omitted any provider-side auto-selected defaults (like Fireworks' auto-selected learning_rate), making the logged config insufficient to actually reproduce the run.

requirement.rule: This config log file must be written to the same output directory the trainer's checkpoints are already saved to, not a new separate logging directory, so a user archiving one directory captures both the checkpoints and the config that produced them together.
requirement.scope: File location.

tasks.title: Code executor stdout/stderr size capping
tasks.description: Cap the amount of stdout/stderr captured from generated code executed via any `CodeExecutor` backend, to prevent a runaway print loop from exhausting memory while collecting output.

requirement.rule: The cap must be enforced as a streaming limit during execution (stop retaining further output once the cap is hit, while letting the process continue running until its own timeout/completion) rather than capturing all output in memory first and truncating it afterward, since the latter approach is exactly the OOM risk this ticket exists to prevent.
requirement.scope: Streaming vs post-hoc truncation, applies to all four backends' output capture.

hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: A first draft captured full output into an in-memory buffer and truncated the final string before returning it, which was reversed once it was pointed out that this didn't actually fix the OOM risk — the runaway print loop would still exhaust memory building the buffer before truncation ever happened.

requirement.rule: When output is truncated due to the cap, the returned result must include a clear marker (e.g. an appended `[output truncated, N bytes omitted]` note) so users can distinguish a truncated-but-otherwise-successful run from one whose real output was genuinely short.
requirement.scope: Truncation marker in returned result.

tasks.title: Litellm backend rate limit config validation against provider minimums
tasks.description: Warn (not error) when a user configures `max_requests_per_minute` or `max_tokens_per_minute` for the litellm backend below a sensible minimum that would make meaningful progress on a large dataset impractically slow.

requirement.rule: This must be a warning printed once at `LLM.__init__` time, never a hard validation error that blocks construction — a user might have a legitimate reason (e.g. a very restrictive shared API key) for an intentionally low rate limit, and this ticket's job is only to flag a likely-unintentional misconfiguration, not to enforce a policy.
requirement.scope: Severity/blocking behavior of this check.
requirement.exclusions_or_crossover: Must not raise or refuse to construct the LLM object under any rate-limit value, however low.

hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: An early draft treated an extremely low rate limit as a hard construction-time error requiring the user to explicitly override a flag to proceed, which was reversed since it blocked legitimate low-rate-limit use cases behind an extra required flag most users wouldn't know to add.

requirement.rule: The 'sensible minimum' threshold used for this warning must be a named constant, not a magic number inlined at the check site, so it can be tuned later without hunting through the codebase for where the check lives.
requirement.scope: Code style/location for the threshold constant.

tasks.title: Trainer sample() prompt formatting consistency with training format
tasks.description: Ensure `TinkerTrainer.sample()` and `FireworksTrainer.sample()` format the input prompt using the same chat-template logic that `format_example()` used during training, so sampled outputs reflect the model's actual fine-tuned behavior rather than being subtly out-of-distribution due to a formatting mismatch.

requirement.rule: `sample()` must reuse the exact same chat-template rendering path `format_example()` invoked during `.train()` (not reimplement a second, parallel prompt-formatting function for the sampling code path), since any divergence between the two would mean the model is sampled with a differently-formatted prompt than it was trained on, silently degrading output quality in a way that would be hard for users to diagnose.
requirement.scope: Prompt formatting code reuse between train() and sample() paths, both trainers.

hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: An early implementation wrote sample()'s prompt formatting independently (a simpler, single-turn-only formatter) since it seemed like sample() only needed to handle simple prompts, which was reversed once it was noticed this diverged from the (potentially multi-turn, system-prompt-including) format_example() logic used in training.

requirement.rule: If a user has subclassed the trainer and overridden `format_example()` with custom logic, `sample()` must call that same overridden method's formatting logic (via the instance, not the base class), so the reuse requirement above also holds for custom subclasses, not just the default implementation.
requirement.scope: Polymorphic dispatch for custom subclasses.

tasks.title: Prompt caching key stability across curator version upgrades
tasks.description: Ensure the cache key format used by `curator.LLM` includes a library-version-scoped namespace, so that upgrading curator to a new version whose prompt-rendering or request-construction logic changed doesn't silently return stale cache hits from an incompatible earlier version.

requirement.rule: The version scope used in the cache key must be tied to a dedicated 'cache format version' constant maintained specifically for this purpose (bumped only when a change would actually affect cached content), not the full package version string, since bumping the cache key on every routine patch release (most of which don't touch caching-relevant logic) would needlessly invalidate the entire cache on every upgrade.
requirement.scope: Choice of version identifier used in the cache key namespace.

hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: A first draft used the full curator package version string directly in the cache key, which was reversed after it caused every user's entire cache to be invalidated on routine patch upgrades that had nothing to do with caching behavior, defeating much of caching's value.

requirement.rule: Old cache entries under a stale cache-format-version namespace must not be actively deleted by this change — they should simply become unreachable (cache misses) and are left for a separate, future cache-pruning task, since implementing pruning here would be out of this ticket's scope.
requirement.scope: Old-entry cleanup scope.
requirement.exclusions_or_crossover: Do not implement automatic pruning/deletion of stale-namespace cache entries as part of this task.

tasks.title: Anonymized telemetry event batching before send
tasks.description: Batch multiple telemetry events together and send them periodically instead of firing an individual network request per event, to reduce overhead on very short-lived scripts that generate many small events.

requirement.rule: On process exit (including normal exit and common signal-based termination), any telemetry events still sitting in the batch buffer must be flushed synchronously before the process actually exits, using an exit-hook mechanism, rather than being silently dropped because the periodic batching timer never got another chance to fire.
requirement.scope: Exit-time flush behavior for the telemetry batching buffer.

hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: The first version relied solely on the periodic timer to eventually send batched events, with no exit hook, which was reversed after it was noticed short-lived scripts (the exact case this batching change was meant to help) were losing nearly all their telemetry events since the process exited before the timer ever fired.

requirement.rule: The exit-time flush must itself still respect `TELEMETRY_ENABLED` at flush time (re-checked at the moment of flush, per the existing rule that this variable is re-evaluated live rather than cached) — if a user disabled telemetry mid-session, the exit flush must discard the buffered events rather than sending them.
requirement.scope: Interaction between exit-flush and the TELEMETRY_ENABLED live-check behavior established elsewhere.
